strengths: Entity-vectors-in-v1 decision is consistently propagated on its own axis: brain-entities appears in §3.2 (with independent per-index 10M-vector and 50k-namespace ceilings, correctly counted separately from brain-chunks), the §6.2 embed-entities Workflow step (vector.id==entities.id, namespace=tenantId, per-row embedded_at/embedding_model), §5.2, §6.6/§6.7 search_entities, §10.1 ENTITY_INDEX binding, and §10.4 provisioning — the sweep's primary target is clean.

Workflows 1 MiB non-stream step-output cap is handled correctly and pervasively: extract-text returns only an R2 staging key + byte size, chunk-text stages chunk content to R2 and returns lean metadata, embed/KG steps read content back from D1/R2 by id, and §6.2 entity steps return counts-only — with the documented ReadableStream<Uint8Array> escape hatch explicitly acknowledged.

Workflow step-budget reasoning is sound against real limits: 10,000-step default (correctly noted as raisable to 25,000 via workflows[].limits.steps on Workers Paid, and explicitly NOT assuming the raise) bounded by MAX_CHUNKS_PER_DOC=4000 with deterministic parent_document_id split, plus a MAX_BODY_BYTES=8MiB second key so few-but-huge chunks can't over-load a part.

Vectorize topK semantics are correct and load-bearing: topK max 100, dropping to 50 only when returnValues:true or returnMetadata:'all' is set — the query sets neither (returns {id,score}), so full topK=100 is available even with a metadata filter; the recall-cliff fix (fold granted scope into the metadata filter via $in rather than over-fetch) is the right call given 100 is a hard ceiling.

AI Gateway enforcement-boundary analysis is precise and correctly grounded: AI Gateway is invoked via the gateway option on env.AI.run (not a wrangler binding); native @cf/ neuron-billed Workers AI calls are covered by neither Unified Billing nor BYOK spend-limit rails, so the enforcing per-tenant cap is the app-level token_spend 429 pre-check BEFORE env.AI.run, with gateway metadata retained only for attribution — and Workers AI request-RATE limits are correctly treated as a separate axis (degrade-or-queue, not user 429).

D1 100-bound-parameter limit is respected (CHUNK_DB_BATCH_SIZE=10 at ~8 params/row; BFS frontier IN(...) chunked at ~90 ids), EMBED_BATCH_SIZE=50 against the bge-m3 per-call cap, and the namespace=tenantId framing is correctly characterized as a query-time partition (same class as a metadata filter), explicitly NOT a documented security boundary, with the D1 row re-check as the authoritative gate.

reviews.summary: The entity-vectors-in-v1 sweep IS clean on its own axis: brain-entities is consistently propagated across §3.2 (independent per-index 10M-vector / 50k-namespace ceilings), the §6.2 embed-entities Workflow step, §5.2, §6.6/§6.7 search_entities, and the §10.1 ENTITY_INDEX binding + §10.4 provisioning. The genuinely strong CF-primitive reasoning is intact and correct against real V2 limits: the 1 MiB non-stream step-output cap is handled by R2-staging the body/chunks and returning counts-only (§4.3/§6.2) with the ReadableStream escape hatch noted; MAX_CHUNKS_PER_DOC=4000 keeps total steps under the 10k default (raisable to 25k via workflows[].limits.steps); D1's 100-bound-param limit drives CHUNK_DB_BATCH_SIZE=10; topK=100 (correctly noted to drop to 50 only with returnValues/returnMetadata:'all', which the query sets neither) with $in multi-scope folding and the 64B metadata/namespace caveat; and the AI Gateway enforcement-boundary analysis (native @cf/ neuron calls are NOT covered by spend limits, so the app-level token_spend 429 pre-check is the enforcing cap) is precise. BUT the re-score uncovers two UNRESOLVED critical straggler classes of exactly the internal-contradiction type that dragged the prior 57 down — the sweep closed the entity-vectors axis but left these open. (1) trust_grade-as-Vectorize-metadata: §3.2/§3.1.1/§4.3 emphatically state trust_grade is NOT a Vectorize metadata index and NOT in the upsert blob (sidecar-only, so a promotion never re-upserts a vector), yet §10.4 line 4181 emits a LIVE `wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index brain-chunks --property-name=trust_grade` (a second provisioning block disagreeing with §3.2's), §10.6/4293 repeats it in the deploy checklist, §8.3/3571 actually UPSERTS metadata {trust_grade:'evidence'} into Vectorize, and §5.3.2/§7.4/§7.9 carry it as a query filter and D1 re-check key — §5.3.2 even self-contradicts (line 1781 filter type has trust_grade?:string while line 1845 says foldPartitionFilter folds only scope/visibility). (2) brain-entities missing from every §10.2 environment override: lines 4131-4132 declare only vectorize:[{index_name:'brain-chunks(-staging)'}] for staging AND production; since wrangler env vectorize arrays REPLACE the top-level array, staging/production would deploy with no ENTITY_INDEX binding, so every embed-entities step and search_entities call throws at runtime — a deploy-breaking gap, and the §10.2 prose (line 4127) still says each env has 'its own brain-chunks Vectorize index' (singular). Both are squarely CF-primitive-correctness within the two-Vectorize-index reality. Per the lens rule, these unresolved criticals cap the score below 60. Two MEDIUMs: §10.1 vars SYNTHESIS_TOKEN_BUDGET='20000' is dead (unread) — §5.5 hardcodes MODEL_CTX_TOKENS=24_000 and derives the budget internally; and §3.2's reserved 5th `source` metadata slot is never actually provisioned/used.

reviews.summary: The entity-vectors-in-v1 decision is now coherent and consistent end-to-end. All four mandated checkpoints pass: §10.1 wrangler declares ENTITY_INDEX→brain-entities, §10.4 provisions brain-entities + its 4 metadata indexes before first filtered upsert, §4.5/§6.2 EntityExtractionWorkflow has a v1 embed-entities step (embed canonical_name+description via bge-m3 → upsert brain-entities, vector.id==entities.id, namespace=tenantId), and §1.7/§2.7/§5.2/§5.3/§6.6/§6.7/§9.2.2 uniformly describe brain-entities + search_entities as IN v1. Every surviving "deferred to Phase 3.5" hit is correctly and exclusively scoped to cross-session SEMANTIC fact/entity dedup (nearest-vector merge) — never the index or search. The §6.6 re-extract cleanup deletes orphaned entity vectors against a live v1 index; §6.7 flow A′ defines the scoped search_entities pipeline (metadata-filter gate + D1 re-check + optional entity_fts RRF). The two internal contradictions that dragged the prior 57 (index/search deferral language) are demonstrably resolved. What holds it short of a clean bill: ONE medium-severity survivor of exactly the class the sweep targeted — §3.2 (line 1063) claims "§10.7 now tracks both indexes' vector + namespace ceilings" and §3.2 line 1062 names the brain-entities-{shard}/tenant_shards.entity_index sharding path (and the entity_index schema column exists at lines 824/2674), yet §10.7's actual headroom-alert response (line 4310) only repoints chunk_index/brain-chunks-{shard}. Plus one low wording straggler (line 4325 "Phase 3.5 entity vectors" should read "entity-vector dedup"). Cleared as deliberate, not oversight: line 2115 defers a private-entity node-space TIER ({world,team} only in v1), which is an allowed scope decision, not an index/search deferral — search over {world,team} entities is correctly v1.

strengths: Break-glass read is exemplary: all four gates (role/explicit-signal/audit+alert/default-path-unchanged) specified concretely in §7.6, listed in the §9.2.2 admin catalog, fails closed to 403 for non-admins, never bypasses tenant_id, and is locked by dedicated canaries #14 (fail-closed) and #15 (returns content AND writes audit+alert)

Entity (brain-entities) search arm is held to the same isolation contract as the chunk arm by construction: ScopedVectorize namespace=tenantId, scope/visibility folded into the metadata filter, and the authoritative D1 re-check on entities via scopePredicate + {world,team} visibilityPredicate; the EdgeSpec/ENTITY_GRAPH parameterization makes the node gate ride automatically on list_entities/get_entity/find_orphans/traverse, with canary #13 as a required merge check

The two-axis separation (allowedScopes = data partition vs capabilities = read/write/admin) is now consistently enforced and explained across §1.4, §7.2, §9.0.1 — the earlier single-scopes collapse is genuinely removed, and the API-key branch correctly routes stored scopes JSON to capabilities (not allowedScopes)

trust_grade is correctly excluded from every actual upsert write blob (§4.3 line 1359-1362, §4.9 line 1542) and from the canonical §3.2 index list — the runtime write path never leaks it into a vector, so the defect is confined to provisioning text

Drop-don't-error / D1-as-existence-authority is applied uniformly across cross-tenant, cross-scope, and intra-tenant-visibility paths, with a 15-row table-driven canary suite and a meta-test that fails if a new surface is added without a canary row

reviews.summary: Ruthless multi-tenant + intra-tenant isolation re-score after the entity-vectors-in-v1 consistency sweep. Three of the four lens checks land cleanly on the canonical spine: (b) the admin break-glass read is fully and correctly specified — role-gated (owner/admin via requireRole('admin')), fail-CLOSED (non-admin + breakGlass:true → 403, no fall-through), audited in the same db.batch (action='breakglass_read' with target principal in diff) plus a guaranteed high-severity alert, tenant_id never bypassed, present in the §9.2.2 admin catalog and exercised by canaries #14/#15; (c) the brain-entities search arm carries the identical tenant+scope/visibility gate as the chunk arm (ScopedVectorize namespace=tenantId, foldPartitionFilter on scope/visibility, authoritative D1 re-check via scopePredicate + {world,team} visibilityPredicate, canary #13), with the EdgeSpec parameterization (§6.1) and §3.2/§6.6/§6.7/§9.2.2 all in agreement.
